title: Scaling Transformers for Discriminative Recommendation via Generative Pretraining

problem.claim: Discriminative recommendation models for CTR and CVR prediction face overfitting caused by data sparsity, and the problem worsens as models become larger.

gap.claim: Larger discriminative models can underperform smaller ones, limiting the scalability of recommendation models.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes GPSD, a framework that uses parameters from a pretrained generative model to initialize a discriminative model and then applies sparse parameter freezing.
GPSD is reported to narrow the generalization gap and maintain performance gains as Transformer dense parameters scale from 13K to 0.3B.
The findings support applying techniques established for large language models to recommendation models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance on industrial-scale and publicly available datasets.
The authors report remarkable improvements in online A/B tests.
The authors report consistent performance improvements as dense parameters scale from 13K to 0.3B, closely following power laws.

narrative_sequence.summary: Discriminative recommendation tasks are important in large-scale recommender-system ranking.
Data sparsity causes overfitting, which becomes worse for larger discriminative models.
GPSD addresses the issue through generative pretraining followed by sparse parameter freezing.
The authors report gains across industrial, public, and online A/B-test settings.
The reported scaling behavior suggests closer integration of recommendation and language-model architectures and techniques.

source_observation.claim: The authors report consistent gains as dense model parameters scale from 13K to 0.3B.

interpretation.claim: A training strategy that preserves scaling benefits may be more useful than simply enlarging a discriminative model.

application.claim: When scaling recommendation models, measure performance across model sizes rather than assuming larger discriminative models will improve results.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the scaling protocol, baselines, or conditions needed to assess the generality of the reported power-law behavior.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the pretrained generative model architecture, training data, or pretraining objective.
The abstract does not identify dataset sizes, baseline models, evaluation metrics, or statistical details for the experiments.
The abstract does not describe the online A/B-test design, duration, or measured outcomes.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility of the reported results.
